overview: Identify hail and wind damage accurately, differentiate from wear, and document collateral to build strong claims.
learningObjectives: Recognize hail and wind indicators on shingles
Differentiate storm damage from normal wear

sections.title: Hail Damage
sections.content: Circular divots, granule loss, exposed mat, fractures; soft metal dents; impact marks on hard surfaces.

sections.title: Wind Damage
sections.content: Lifted/creased/missing shingles, directional patterns, exposed nail heads, flashing/trim damage.

sections.title: Collateral Assessment
sections.content: Screens, gutters, downspouts, window wraps, all metal components, siding damage.

sections.title: Documentation Strategy
sections.content: ID → overview → elevation collateral → roof overview → circle hail / slash wind → majority damage overview → granules in gutters/downspouts.

quiz.question: Why is collateral important?
quiz.correctAnswer: It corroborates storm causation and strengthens the claim.
